en.name: Turmeric, fresh
en.summary: Fresh turmeric keeps 2–5 days at room temperature, 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 6 months in the freezer. The physiology behind that is well documented for rhizomes; the numbers themselves are borrowed from fresh ginger root, which is the same kind of rhizome in the form a home cook buys it.
en.pantry: 2–5 days in a cool, dark, airy spot. Turmeric is a tropical rhizome and, like ginger, is chilling sensitive below about 12 °C (54 °F), so a few days out of the fridge does it no harm at all — in fact the rhizome would rather be at 12 to 14 °C than at fridge temperature. What it does do in a dry kitchen is dehydrate and shrivel quickly, so keep it out of a draught and out of the sun. Commercial cured-rhizome storage at those warmer temperatures with high humidity runs to 60 or 90 days, but those are not conditions a kitchen can reproduce.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks unpeeled, in a paper bag or a loosely closed box in the crisper. Cold is a compromise: the fridge is well below the 12 to 14 °C the rhizome actually wants, so expect skin darkening and pitting eventually — that is chilling injury, not rot. In exchange it holds off mould and shrivelling for a couple of weeks, which is usually the right trade in a home kitchen. Watch the cut ends, where condensation collects and mould starts. It stains everything it touches, cutting board and fingers included.
en.freezer: 6 months. Freeze it whole and unpeeled, then grate it from frozen — much the easiest way to handle turmeric, with no loss of colour and none of the staining that comes from wrestling with a wet rhizome. Bag it airtight with the air pressed out. A frozen rhizome grates on a microplane straight into a curry, a dal or a hot drink.
en.thawing: Do not thaw — grate or slice it straight from frozen. A thawed rhizome goes soft and watery and is far messier to work with.
spoilage: Soft, wet patches or a shrivelled, hollow feel.
Mould at the cut ends, where condensation collects.
Dry, woody flesh that no longer stains when cut.
A musty or fermented smell instead of a fresh, peppery, earthy one.
tips: Freeze whole and grate from frozen; it is far easier and far less messy.
Wear gloves or use the back of a spoon to peel; turmeric stains skin and boards.
Do not wash it before storing — surface moisture is what starts the mould.
Buy firm rhizomes with taut skin; a shrivelled one is already on its way out.

faq.q: How long does fresh turmeric keep?
faq.a: 2–5 days at room temperature, 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 6 months in the freezer. These figures are read across from fresh ginger root.
Yes, 6 months. Freeze it whole and unpeeled and grate it from frozen; the colour and flavour hold up and it is much less messy.

faq.q: Does fresh turmeric need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not for the first few days. It is chilling sensitive, so it is happier at around 12 to 14 °C, but the fridge is the practical compromise for a longer window.

zh.name: 新鮮薑黃
zh.summary: 新鮮薑黃放常溫可放 2～5 天，放 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週，冷凍 6 個月。背後的生理學對根莖類有完整的文獻依據；但數字本身是從新鮮生薑借來的——同樣是根莖，而且是一般人買得到的型態。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光、通風的位置，2～5 天。薑黃是熱帶根莖，和薑一樣在大約 12 °C（54 °F）以下會有冷害，所以離開冰箱放幾天完全沒問題——事實上它比較想待在 12 到 14 °C，而不是冰箱的溫度。它在乾燥廚房裡真正會發生的事，是快速脫水、皺縮，所以請避開風口和陽光。商業上的熟化根莖倉儲在那個較高的溫度與高濕度下可達 60 到 90 天，但那不是家裡廚房能重現的條件。
zh.fridge: 不削皮，用紙袋或蓋不緊的盒子放蔬果室，2～3 週。低溫是一種妥協：冰箱遠低於這個根莖真正想要的 12 到 14 °C，所以久了會出現表皮變深與凹點——那是冷害，不是腐爛。交換來的是它兩週內不太會發霉或皺縮，對家庭廚房來說通常是划算的。請盯著切口，那裡會積結露，霉也從那裡開始。它碰到什麼就染什麼，砧板和手指都不例外。
zh.freezer: 6 個月。整塊不削皮直接冷凍，要用時從冷凍狀態直接刨——這是處理薑黃最輕鬆的方式，顏色不會掉，也免去跟一塊濕根莖搏鬥時弄得到處都是的麻煩。請壓出空氣密封裝袋。冷凍的薑黃用細刨刀可以直接刨進咖哩、扁豆湯或熱飲裡。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍——直接從冷凍刨或切。解凍後的根莖會變軟出水，處理起來更髒亂。
spoilage: 出現軟塌濕爛的斑塊，或摸起來乾癟中空。
切口長霉，那裡最容易積結露。
肉質乾硬木質化，切開也不再染色。
聞起來有霉味或發酵味，而不是清新帶胡椒感的土香。
tips: 整塊冷凍、從冷凍直接刨；省事得多，也乾淨得多。
削皮時戴手套或用湯匙背刮；薑黃會染手也會染砧板。
存放前不要洗——表面的水正是發霉的起點。
挑結實、表皮緊繃的；已經皺縮的等於走在下坡路上。

faq.a: 常溫 2～5 天，4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週，冷凍 6 個月。這些數字是比照新鮮生薑而來。
可以，6 個月。整塊不削皮冷凍，要用時直接刨；顏色與風味都撐得住，也乾淨得多。
頭幾天不需要。它怕冷，其實比較適合 12 到 14 °C；但要撐比較久的話，冰箱是務實的妥協。
